display.title: Episode 347: The Invisible Aleph and the Rebbe Rayatz's Teacher
display.summary_short: Turn your house into a mitzvah with a tzedakah pushka, a first-grade class leads the Shema, the hunt for the invisible Aleph, and a story of the young Rebbe Rayatz and his teacher.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the week of Parshas Noach 5749. Uncle Yossi explains that 'mitzvah' also means connection, so fixing your tzedakah pushka permanently to a wall turns your whole house into a great mitzvah that helps bring Moshiach; children are invited to write in describing how they did it, with prizes for the first letters. After the Hakochainik march and the sponsor, a first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school leads the Shema. Then comes a hunt for the 'invisible Aleph': why do the Torah and every brachah begin with a Beis? The Aleph, which stands for one, is Hashem Echad, unseen but always present. A story shows how to say 'Baruch Atah': the ten-year-old Yosef Yitzchak, later the Frierdiker Rebbe, saw his teacher, the Radatz, cover his forehead before every brachah, and learned that the Tzemach Tzedek had taught him as a child to stop and think before Whom he is saying it. A dive into the mailbox brings a letter about returning lost eyeglasses, and the show ends with Shabbos candle time.
display.lesson: Before every brachah, stop and think to Whom you are speaking: Hashem Echad, the invisible Aleph who is always right here.
